title: Vicky Kaushal Has Blocked 18 Months of His Life for One Film. It's About an Immortal Who Hasn't Finished His Work.
excerpt: The actor will spend six months transforming his body and mind before a year-long shoot for Mahavatar, Maddock Films' mythological epic about Lord Parashurama. No other projects. No distractions.
body:
In an industry where top actors routinely juggle three or four projects in a single calendar year, Vicky Kaushal has made a choice that reads like a statement. He has blocked 18 months — a year and a half — exclusively for one film. No side projects. No guest appearances. No brand shoots squeezed between schedules. Just Mahavatar.

## The Scale of the Commitment

The math alone is staggering. Starting this month, Kaushal enters a six-month preparatory phase that includes a complete physical transformation and intensive workshops designed by director Amar Kaushik. The goal: to inhabit the body and mind of Chiranjeevi Parashurama, the sixth avatar of Lord Vishnu, one of the seven Immortals of Hindu mythology.

When principal photography begins in January 2027, Kaushal intends to stay on set exclusively until the film wraps in December. That is 12 months of continuous production — a timeline that mirrors the schedules of Hollywood tentpoles but is virtually unheard of in Hindi cinema, where even ambitious historical epics like Padmaavat and Baahubali were shot over fragmented schedules spanning years.

Kaushal is expected to wrap his current commitment — Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Love and War, co-starring Ranbir Kapoor and Alia Bhatt — by late June, with Bhansali targeting a 50-day schedule that aims for a January 21, 2027 release. The handoff from one demanding filmmaker to another is seamless by design.

## The Director and the Studio

Amar Kaushik is not an obvious choice for a mythological epic. He built his reputation through the Stree horror-comedy franchise, which became one of India's most commercially successful film series. But Maddock Films — the studio behind Stree, Stree 2, and the expanding horror universe — has positioned Mahavatar as its most ambitious production ever.

Kaushik has confirmed that pre-production has consumed the better part of a year. "The prep is going on for 6-7 months," he told Bollywood Hungama. "We have worked on the set design, weapon design, how every character would look. The scripting is done. Yet, we need more time." That pursuit of time — rather than rushing to capitalize on Kaushal's post-Chhaava star power — signals that Maddock is betting on quality over speed.

Reports indicate Shraddha Kapoor is the frontrunner for the female lead, which would mark her first collaboration with Kaushal. Given both actors' commercial pull — Shraddha with the Stree franchise, Kaushal with Uri, Chhaava, and Love and War — the pairing carries significant box office promise.

## Why Parashurama, and Why Now

The character of Parashurama occupies a unique space in Hindu mythology. Unlike Ram or Krishna, whose stories have been told repeatedly on screen, Parashurama is the avatar who never died. He is a Chiranjeevi — an Immortal — who appears across multiple yugas, carrying an axe given to him by Lord Shiva, sworn to eliminate corruption wherever he finds it.

For the Indian diaspora, the timing matters. There is a global appetite for mythological storytelling that has been validated by the success of films rooted in Indian epics. Rajamouli's Varanasi project with Mahesh Babu and Priyanka Chopra, Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana, and now Mahavatar represent a new wave of Indian cinema that treats its mythological source material with the budget and ambition previously reserved for Marvel or DC properties.

## The Industry Trend

Kaushal's 18-month lockout is the most extreme example of a growing pattern. Ranveer Singh's Pralay begins an August 2026 shoot. Mahesh Babu has been exclusively committed to Rajamouli's project. Prabhas spent years on Kalki 2898 AD. The common thread: India's biggest male stars are choosing depth over volume, betting that one transformative role is worth more than three safe ones.

The film was originally slated for Christmas 2026 but has been pushed to 2027, with Independence Day weekend as the most likely target. Maddock's own Stree 3 may have to shift to accommodate it — a sign of which project the studio considers its priority.

For Kaushal, the calculation is simple. He has played a soldier, a Maratha warrior, and a romantic lead for Bhansali. Playing an Immortal requires something more than preparation. It requires surrender. Eighteen months is the price of that surrender.
author: Diaspora Desk
